📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 08:02 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 10:36 EST, 16 November 2026.

Jurgen Klopp has called on FIFA's embattled president Gianni Infantino to resign, becoming the first national team manager to do so.

Infantino's reputation took a nosedive after his sycophantic behaviour towards Donald Trump before and during the World Cup - most memorably by awarding him a 'FIFA Peace Prize'.

And it only got worse when his clandestine plot to sell off stakes in the World Cup, a devious scheme which would have banked him millions, was revealed by The Times.

Now Germany manager Klopp has hit out: 'There is now a unanimous consensus that a change would make sense.

'I thought that, after Sepp Blatter, the situation couldn't get any worse - but here we are.

'Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job.

Jurgen Klopp has publicly savaged FIFA president Gianni Infantino, becoming the first national team manager to do so.

The Germany manager remarked Infantino - who tried to sell off stakes in the World Cup to his own benefit - is 'worse' than his predecessor Sepp Blatter.

'Without a doubt, there are people who truly care about football and have no financial interests,' the former Liverpool manager noted.

Infantino has clung on to his job thus far, surviving a crisis summit in Morocco in August, despite intense and widespread opposition.

A total of 90 nations including all of UEFA's teams rebelled, with threats to boycott FIFA competitions, and Infantino's £3.1billion proposal fell apart.

Sources indicate that but he still maintained a large swell of support among Africa, Asia, and South America - especially after offering each nation £30million if they supported his plan. His opponents pointed out that he could simply have given money from FIFA's cash reserves of roughly £4.5b.

In the pages of this historic newspaper, football legend Luis Figo wrote that 'Infantino must go' and accused him of 'debasing the office of FIFA President'.

FIFA does not have a history of picking good leaders - Blatter resigned in 2015 amid allegations of corruption, though he was cleared alongside Michel Platini last year.

Infantino now looks well-placed to be re-elected for a fourth term in next March's presidential elections.

The deadline for candidacies to be submitted is November 18.

Philippe Diallo, the French Football Federation president, has agreed to run against Infantino and has the backing of UEFA's executive committee.

'(Diallo has) extensive experience across all levels of the game, having led the organisation representing French professional football clubs, served on the board of the French professional league and within FIFA’s dispute resolution structures, before becoming President of the FFF and a member of the UEFA Executive Committee in 2023,' UEFA said.

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega has already announced his intention to be a rival to Infantino.

Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japanese Football Association, is also reportedly set to mount a challenge.

Ex-Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger was touted as a potential challenger but it is understood he told European football’s governing body UEFA that he would not stand.

Dundee vs Hearts - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 11:25, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 11:33.
  • Without a win in any competition for almost a month, under-pressure Wouter Vrancken takes his Hearts side to Dens Park this weekend to face Dundee as the Scottish Premiership returns following the international break.
  • The Dee headed into the international break in fifth place after a narrow 2-1 defeat to St Johnstone, while the Jambos suffered a third consecutive loss after being thrashed 5-2 at home by an in-form Falkirk side.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 11:25, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 11:33.

Without a win in any competition for almost a month, under-pressure Wouter Vrancken takes his Hearts side to Dens Park this weekend to face Dundee as the Scottish Premiership returns following the international break.

The Dee headed into the international break in fifth place after a narrow 2-1 defeat to St Johnstone, while the Jambos suffered a third consecutive loss after being thrashed 5-2 at home by an in-form Falkirk side.

After a relatively quiet end to the 2025-26 season, during which Dundee neither threatened relegation nor came close to securing European football, Steven Pressley entered the new campaign hoping to take his side a step further.

Now approaching his 18th month in charge at Dens Park, Pressley has overseen five wins, two draws and five defeats in the opening 12 matches of the 2026-27 season, leaving the Dee fifth in the table and with an opportunity to leapfrog their upcoming opponents with a victory on Saturday afternoon.

Dundee won just one of their four matches leading up to the international break, a comfortable victory over bottom side Kilmarnock, while a draw against Rangers and 2-1 defeats to St Mirren and St Johnstone suggest the two-week stoppage may have come at a welcome time for Pressley's side.

A key factor behind their early-season fortunes has been their solid defensive record, with the side based on the north bank of the Firth of Tay conceding just 15 goals in their opening 12 Scottish Premiership outings, making their latest defeat all the more frustrating.

Dundee suffered an error-strewn defeat in the Tayside derby in Perth at the start of the month, losing 2-1 to St Johnstone, and will know that individual mistakes have prevented them from climbing further up the table.

Despite their inconsistent form, the Dee remain just four points behind third-placed Falkirk, with a game in hand, and will know that a victory against a depleted Hearts side this weekend could further strengthen their impressive start to the campaign.

As for the visitors, Hearts make the journey north from the Scottish capital on the back of three consecutive defeats across the Scottish League Cup, Conference League and Scottish Premiership.

Their cup run came to an end against rivals Hibernian before a 3-1 defeat to Swiss side Thun left them without a European victory all season, with a 5-2 league loss to high-flying Falkirk just days later only increasing the pressure on Vrancken.

An injury-hit Hearts side entered their latest Scottish Premiership fixture hoping to extend their 26-match unbeaten run at Tynecastle Park, but were left stunned after falling 4-0 behind at half-time before eventually losing 5-2, allowing John McGlynn's side to replace the Jambos in third place.

The humiliating defeat, which the Belgian boss described as "embarrassing" and a "disgrace", leaves Hearts 11 points behind league leaders Celtic, having held a seven-point advantage this time last year, and entering the final international break of the year knowing they need a significant points haul to get their campaign back on track.

A demanding 39-day period in which Hearts will play 11 matches before the end of the calendar year leaves precious little time for recovery, with their challenging schedule including encounters against Celtic and Rangers, another Edinburgh derby and three further Conference League fixtures in a league phase where their hopes of qualification are fading.

One positive for the Jambos is that they have won their last four meetings with Dundee, most recently coming from behind to secure a 2-1 victory in September thanks to two late goals, the second of which arrived in the 96th minute.

Hearts form (all competitions):.

Dundee entered the international break without any further injury concerns following their defeat to St Johnstone and could therefore name an unchanged starting XI, although Pressley may be tempted to make alterations after some of his half-time substitutes impressed.

Joe Westley made an immediate impact after coming on at half-time, scoring less than three minutes later, and could now earn a starting place at the expense of either Ashley Hay or Bradley Fink.

Bobby Wales has not featured for the Dee in more than two months but is gradually working his way back to fitness and could make the matchday squad this weekend, although he will not be joined by Finlay Robertson or Simon Murray, who are both expected to remain sidelined until August 2027.

Meanwhile, Hearts' recent struggles could be partly put down to their ongoing injury crisis.

The Jambos are once again expected to be without as many as 11 players, with the Edinburgh-based side hoping to avoid any further setbacks before the January transfer window.

Players such as Stephen Kingsley, Tomas Magnusson and Blair Spittal are expected to return in the coming weeks, while Harry Milne and Calvin Miller are likely to remain sidelined for several months.

Both sides have managed just two wins between them across their last four matches and will be desperate to enter the festive period with some positive momentum.

With little separating the teams in the table, we expect that to be reflected on the pitch, with the pair playing out a low-scoring draw as Scottish Premiership action resumes.

Lethal Trent Alexander-Arnold sends Tuchel a statement in England victory

📅 29 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 32 min read (6356 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~32 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.
  • In a recent development, england always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie.
  • TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.

In a recent development, england always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie. This was the first cap in 15 months for the right-back now known simply as “Trent” in an England shirt – as well as his Real Madrid jersey – rather than the six syllables of his surname. With the game level at half-time, two minutes into the new half, he twice won the ball before landing a cross on the head of Anthony Gordon for the first goal.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24.

According to recent reports, will the Alexander-Arnold with England experiment survive? One feels that Tuchel will need a little more to convince him to abandon whatever reservations he has about the Liverpudlian. A week short of his 28th birthday, Alexander-Arnold was winning just his 35th cap. His Real Madrid team-mate Jude Bellingham, a second-half substitute, was earning his 58th cap less than two months after his 23rd birthday. Bellingham was on as captain in place of the man he replaced, Harry Kane, scorer of England’s second. Bellingham’s international career has taken a much less rocky path than that of his Real team-mate.

It has been revealed that having missed the World Cup finals this summer, and had little good fortune around previous tournaments, one wonders if Euro 2028 might be the watershed moment for Alexander-Arnold. Either way, against opponents who sit back, he is lethal when it is time for the major delivery. Alexander-Arnold may not have the breadth of England experience that some of his peers have accumulated, but he does have plenty of experience of big games.

“I make that run time and time again,” Gordon stated of his anticipation of the Alexander-Arnold cross, “but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him [Alexander-Arnold]. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry – he would have loved to have played more.”.

A Freudian slip from the Barcelona winger, another Liverpudlian in Spain, who himself has barely put a foot wrong for England of late. He has three goals in three games for England, including the World Cup semi-final against Argentina. This was an England team that Tuchel fine-tuned, first to give a rest to Bellingham and in other quarters, too. Lewis Hall started at left-back. Trevoh Chalobah won his third England cap at centre-back. Alex Scott, of Bournemouth, was given his debut off the bench in the second half and Rio Ngumoha won the second cap of his England career, just one month after his 18th birthday.

Industry observers note that as for Kane, his 87th goal for England now puts him within two goals of Robert Lewandowski, among four greats in the seven ahead of Kane on the all-time international goalscorers’ list. By the end of this international break the England captain should have equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps. It has been an astonishing career even if it ends tomorrow. Following the missed penalty against Spain, Kane was again the man in the right place at the right time when Morgan Rogers’s shot was blocked in the second half.

It’s an awkward one, but we kept going, got a win and that’s what counts.” Not quite a vintage Czech Republic team, either, and when their best player of the opening stages, the attacking midfielder Pavel Sulc, of Lyon in Ligue 1, was dismissed after 25 minutes, it certainly did not become any easier for the home team. Sulc, the Czech player of the year in 2025, had mistimed a tackle on Elliot Anderson, which on a VAR review, the Turkish referee Umut Meler decided was worthy of an upgrade from yellow to red. It was high on the right calf of the England midfielder.

England had looked once more a little open to the counter-attack in the early stages, with Sulc one notable runner. This was not an opponent of the quality of Spain and Tuchel’s players were able to recover the situation. When they lose the ball in the opposition’s half, England tend to look vulnerable.

Even before the red card Rogers had hit a post. Myles Lewis-Skelly, playing in midfield, was booked for a foul on Lukas Serv and was pursued thereafter by the Czech players hoping to get an upgrade on the yellow card. He was substituted at half-time, with Eberechi Eze on in his place.

“I spoke to Ant [Gordon] at half-time,” Alexander-Arnold stated later to ITV, “and I said if I’m getting in those spaces make sure you get to the back post. You don’t expect to get it that fast, but it did and it worked.”.

Two minutes after the break, Alexander-Arnold suddenly burst into life. He won the ball back in his own area and then drove forward in search of the return. When that did not come, he raced back to win the ball again and unleashed one of those right-footed outswingers to the back post, where Gordon guided in the header. “Really proud to score that,” Gordon said, “because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.”.

Thomas Tuchel has backed Jude Bellingham as a future England captain after giving him the armband in the victory over the Czech Republic.

In the absence of Declan Rice, who was vice-captain at the World Cup, Bellingham assumed the role when he came on for Harry Kane, who is now in his 10th season as England captain and also scored in the 2-0 win in Prague.

Tuchel, who needs to check on Bellingham ahead of Saturday’s game against Croatia after a “niggle,” has praised the midfielder’s attitude during the extended international break one year after he was back from an injury but left out of the squad.

“If you are the captain at the end of these matches, you can be the permanent captain,” Tuchel stated when asked whether Bellingham could eventually lead the team. “He was the captain against New Zealand before the World Cup. It is always a reward and always an honour.

“I think he loves to be with us at the moment. That’s what I feel, and we had this small talk today about his role. We felt in our hearts or our stomachs to say ‘let’s go again, let’s start again’ and also our heads told us maybe 30 minutes is enough for this match because he hasn’t played in this quick turnaround through this season. He has done it before, but not in the season, so we didn’t want to be the first ones to try that.

Recent findings suggest that “But even in this little encounter, you can see that he’s confident and happy to help from the bench. So it’s a reward. It’s good. He had a little niggle at the end of the match, so hopefully it’s nothing serious, and he’s available for Croatia.”.

Nico O’Reilly is a doubt for the Croatia match in Rijeka and there are also concerns over Ezri Konsa, who was on the bench but not fit enough to play.

The Professional Footballers’ Association has leapt to Cole Palmer’s defence following his withdrawal from the England squad.

The union’s CEO,  Maheta Molango, said the Chelsea forward is a victim of a “sick” system that is demanding too much from players physically.

“When England see five players who need to withdraw when the single most proud moment a player has is to be called up for the national team, you just ask yourself, what’s wrong about the industry?” Molango said at the Fifpro performance summit in London.

“You see people like Cole Palmer, someone who would have played four consecutive summers in a row had he gone to the World Cup, and you wonder why is he missing?”He’s missing because he’s a victim of the calendar and that’s something that needs to absolutely trigger the alarm bells.”.

Trevoh Chalobah will earn his third England cap in tonight’s Nations League match against Czech Republic. The Como centre-back, 27, played in the 6-4 defeat of France in the Bronze final at the World Cup and his other appearance for the Three Lions was in the defeat by Senegal last year.

Sources indicate that trent Alexander-Arnold will make his first England appearance in 15 months after being given a start. The Real Madrid full-back, who was not selected for the World Cup in the summer, earned his last cap against Andorra in 2025.

He replaces Jarell Quansah in Thomas Tuchel’s line-up that lost to Spain at the weekend.

“Trent had a very good training week and the excellent training in Wembley after the match, where he showed that he absolutely wants to play and wants to be with us,” said Tuchel on the eve of the game at Fortuna Arena.

“We’re good. Everything is fine. He’s ready to go. He has qualities that you all know, like he’s strong on the ball, excellent crossing, good finishing. And very, very good on the ball. That’s basically what he brings.”.

Ezri Konsa, who missed team training on the day before this game, is out. Morgan Rogers, meanwhile, steps in for Jude Bellingham in the No10 role as Tuchel looks to juggle four matches in 11 days during this extended international break.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is in line to make his first England start under head coach Thomas Tuchel for tonight’s Nations League game against Czech Republic.

Injuries to Nico O’Reilly and Ezri Konsa have forced Tuchel into changes at the back, with Alexander-Arnold expected to come in at right-back, Trevoh Chalobah to replace Konsa and Lewis Hall to step in for O’Reilly.

Alexander-Arnold has made only one appearance under Tuchel, as a substitute in a World Cup qualifying win against Andorra in June 2025. His last start for England came under interim head coach Lee Carsley, when he scored in a victory over Finland.

Jude Belllingham could be given a rest after playing the full 90 minutes in the defeat by Spain, which would give Morgan Rogers an opportunity in the No 10 position.

Man City used ‘sham’ sponsorships in £830m cheating scheme.

Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Uefa Nations League match between Czech Republic and England from Slavia Prague’s Eden Stadium. The home side, 49th in the Fifa rankings, scrambled their way to World Cup qualification with victories in the play-offs in penalty shoot-outs over Ireland and Denmark, promptly stank Group A out in Mexico/Canada/United States, drawing with South Africa but losing to South Korea and Mexico to finish last.

Miroslav Koubek, their 74-year-old manager, the oldest in the competition’s history, promptly stood down and has been replaced by their first foreign head coach, Santi, the former Atlético Madrid centre-half, who spent 15 years moving from managing Spain’s U17s, to the U19s and then the U21s. Little wonder, given his CV, that he is looking to refresh his squad with a transfusion of young players, a requirement made all the more urgent by the international retirement of stalwart centre-forward Patrick Schick and the absence of West Ham’s Tomas Soucek who damaged his ankle in that 3-0 defeat by Mexico on June 25 and has not kicked a ball since.

Recent findings suggest that santi started his stint in charge and this campaign in Group A3 with a 2-1 defeat by Croatia but there were some very positive signs – they set up as a 4-3-3 in classic Spanish/Cruyff style and pressed like dervishes. England, who conceded three goals when players made mistakes when subjected to aggressive pressing in their opening 3-2 defeat by world champions Spain, will have to find better solutions tonight, either by holding their nerve or counterpressing with fewer mistakes.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, yesterday afternoon, Fikayo Tomori and Ruben Loftus-Cheek underwent examinations to assess their recovery from their respective muscle injuries. The tests took place in London, where both players spent the week off granted by the coaching staff.

The news is encouraging, and the recovery process is progressing well: the injury to the defender’s medial flexor in his right thigh is healing, and he will begin gradual work on the pitch over the coming days.

Industry observers note that whether he will be available against Frosinone or for the Europa League match against Olympiakos remains to be seen. The injury sustained against Bologna in late October is nearly behind him, but no unnecessary risks will be taken.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 11:30, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 11:50.
  • Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca may consider making some bold changes to his starting lineup for Saturday lunchtime’s Premier League clash at home against Fulham.
  • The Citizens have lost their last three top-flight matches, most recently suffering a disappointing 3-1 defeat at Nottingham Forest before the international break in which both Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol were at fault for first-half goals conceded.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 11:30, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 11:50.

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca may consider making some bold changes to his starting lineup for Saturday lunchtime’s Premier League clash at home against Fulham.

The Citizens have lost their last three top-flight matches, most recently suffering a disappointing 3-1 defeat at Nottingham Forest before the international break in which both Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol were at fault for first-half goals conceded.

Both players were taken off at half time due to injury, but while Gvardiol has recovered and represented Croatia during the break, a hip issue forced Guehi to withdraw from England duty and the centre-back has emerged as a doubt for Saturday.

Abdukodir Khusanov did not play for Uzbekistan due to a knock and will also need to be assessed, opening the door for Vitor Reis, 20, to potentially start his first Premier League game under Maresca at the heart of a defence that has conceded 17 goals in the last eight games.

Despite concerns over his recent form, Gianluigi Donnarumma is expected to continue in goal, and captain Ruben Dias should start again at centre-back, while Matheus Nunes and Gvardiol are seemingly the most likely duo to start as full-backs, though the latter faces competition from Nico O’Reilly for the left-back spot.

While Elliot Anderson has established himself as an important first-team midfielder for Man City, there are question marks over Enzo Fernandez’s role under Maresca and the Italian coach may consider swapping him out for Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Rayan Cherki, who has scored five PL goals this season, is likely to retain his starting spot in the number 10 role, forcing Phil Foden to battle with Iliman Ndiaye, Jeremey Doku and Allan for starts out wide.

Erling Haaland is all but certain to lead the line once again; the Norwegian scored three goals in two games for his country in the UEFA Nations League, while he has netted 14 goals in as many matches for Man City across all tournaments this term.

Manchester City possible starting lineup:.

Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Bouaddi; Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku, Haaland.

Breaking: Thomas Frank unveiled as Crystal Palace boss as he eyes raid on Chelsea set-piece guru marginalised under Xabi Alonso

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (506 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER and KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.
  • Published: 10:07 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:08 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Thomas Frank has been unveiled as Crystal Palace’s new manager on a two-and-a-half-year deal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER and KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 10:07 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:08 EST, 16 November 2026.

Thomas Frank has been unveiled as Crystal Palace’s new manager on a two-and-a-half-year deal.

Frank has been out of work since being sacked by Tottenham Hotspur in February and has taken a significant pay cut to take over at Palace, who languish at the bottom of the Premier League.

However, he will earn more than his predecessor, Pierre Sage, who was sacked last week after winning just two of his ten league matches in charge.

Fresh Palace boss Frank mentioned: ‘It's an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic Football Club. I'm really, really looking forward to it.

Sources indicate that ‘Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League. I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them.’.

Across his spells at Brentford and Tottenham, Frank has managed 178 Premier League matches with a 34 per cent win rate.

Palace are set to approach Chelsea about Bernardo Cueva, who worked with Frank at Brentford before being poached to become the Blues' set-piece specialist.

We are pleased to confirm the appointment of Thomas Frank as Manager 🤝ℹ️ https://t.co/2wUzZAGt4S pic.twitter.com/zv2vMPGPFz.

Palace are set to approach Chelsea about Cueva (right), who worked with Frank at Brentford.

Sources indicate that but Cueva may now be elevated back to the forefront of football if Palace can strike an agreement to bring him in to join Frank’s backroom staff. It is stated Chelsea paid Brentford around £1million in compensation to hire him in 2024 at a time when his stock was high.

Cueva arrived at Chelsea in 2024. However, Daily Mail Sport revealed in the last summer how the 39-year-old Mexican’s role was changing after two seasons of work as Xabi Alonso’s side hired Austin MacPhee from Aston Villa as their latest lead on set-plays.

Cueva has not been seen since then, either in training at Cobham or at matches at Stamford Bridge, but continued to work for Chelsea in more of an analytical role behind the scenes.

Club sources stressed at the time that it should not be seen as a demotion, and he is still listed on the first-team staff section of the website under the title ‘technical analyst’.

Chelsea are due to play Palace in two weeks' time at the Bridge on Wednesday, December 2.

Chelsea previously identified Cueva as a prime candidate for a role which had been vacant since Anthony Barry exited for Bayern Munich. Cueva, who also holds a UEFA Pro Licence through the Football Association, was regarded as an impressive acquisition in 2024.

In a recent development, before joining Brentford in 2020 and helping them secure promotion to the Premier League, Cueva was at Chivas in his homeland of Mexico. He has also had a role with Norway men's national team.

After failing to complete their defence in the final days of the summer transfer window, AC Milan will try again in January.

The defensive depth is rather limited amid Matteo Gabbia’s lengthy injury absence, while Fikayo Tomori also sustained an matter, meaning a reinforcement in that area of ​​the pitch will be needed in January. Ruben Amorim’s number one target has not changed from the summer.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, this morning’s edition of Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews) confirms the No.1 centre-back target: Goncalo Inacio. Milan tried to snatch him from Sporting CP in August, but the Portuguese club repeatedly turned them down, having already sold Ousmane Diomande to Nottingham Forest.

Industry observers note that the Rossoneri haven’t abandoned the idea of ​​reuniting him with Amorim, and so in January they will make another attempt for the 25-year-old, who is eager to join a top club. However, a significant offer of at least €40m will be needed to convince Sporting.

The management believe that another central defender is needed too, so they’re starting to monitor some prospects for next summer. Among the players being closely monitored is Gabriele Calvani, who is on loan at Frosinone from Genoa.

Recent findings suggest that he has impressed so far and has a current valuation of €10m that could rise. For now, signing a young prospect isn’t a priority for the Rossoneri, as they are primarily looking for someone who can slot immediately into the starting XI.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 19 Nov 2026 11:34.
  • Millwall play host to Queens Park Rangers on Saturday afternoon looking for the win that would kick-start their playoff bid.
  • At a time when the Lions sit in 16th position in the Championship table, the Hoops make the trip to The Den in eighth place.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 19 Nov 2026 11:34.

Millwall play host to Queens Park Rangers on Saturday afternoon looking for the win that would kick-start their playoff bid.

At a time when the Lions sit in 16th position in the Championship table, the Hoops make the trip to The Den in eighth place.

While Alex Neil has credit in the bank after leading Millwall to last season's playoffs, the Scot knows that may run out at some stage.

Recording just two wins from 10 Championship matches since September 12 could create doubt in the mind of Millwall's hierarchy as they bid to replicate their 2025-26 achievements.

Not only have Millwall posted four defeats in six games, they suffered back-to-back 3-0 defeats to Birmingham City and West Bromwich Albion before the international break.

Furthermore, their only clean sheet during that 10-match period came against bottom-of-the-table Preston North End.

In terms of home form, Millwall have recorded three wins and 11 points from seven games at The Den, but two of those victories have been versus Bolton Wanderers and Derby County, who are 18th and 23rd place respectively.

Although QPR have also been inconsistent of late, they find themselves six points above Millwall in the table.

Five draws have been registered across a 10-game period, yet three wins have come from their last six outings.

Nevertheless, Julien Stephan's side have gone five matches without recording a victory away from Loftus Road, a run that includes successive defeats at Birmingham and Southampton.

Losing at those two clubs will be put into context, but collecting just nine points from seven away fixtures will need to improve in order to keep in contention for promotion.

QPR went into the international break having accumulated four points from home matches with Burnley and Lincoln City.

Queens Park Rangers Championship form:.

As well as Derek Mazou-Sacko being suspended, Neil will inevitably make further changes to his Millwall XI.

Either Daniel Kelly or Casper de Norre, if he has recovered from injury, could return in midfield, while Romain Esse, Mihailo Ivanovic, Tairyk Arconte and Lyndon Dykes are all options for the final third.

The likes of Filip Marschall, Tristan Crama and Ryan Leonard are among those expected to remain on the sidelines.

Nicolas Madsen and Rumarn Burrell are both in line to return to the QPR squad for this fixture.

However, they may have to make do with a place on the substitutes' bench, with Stephan potentially against making alterations for this contest.

That remarked, Ilias Chair and Karamoko Dembele are pushing for opportunities in the final third.

Millwall possible starting lineup:.

Crocombe; Osei-Tutu, Taylor, Cooper, Sturge; Kelly, Metcalfe; Neghli, Cundle, Esse; Ivanovic.

Queens Park Rangers possible starting lineup:.

Charles; Adamson, Edwards, Dunne, Kemper; Varane, Kamara; Chair, Vale, Smyth; Kone.

According to recent reports, while QPR go into this contest in the better form, the international break came at the right time for Millwall. With home advantage in their favour, we feel that they will come through a competitive encounter with three points.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 19 Nov 2026 11:43.
  • Barcelona want to prioritise signing a centre-back in the upcoming winter transfer window, but Hansi Flick also wants a upcoming full-back.
  • Barcelona have won the last two La Liga titles, but have suffered two Champions League failures, in the semi-final against Inter Milan and in the quarter-final against Atletico Madrid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 19 Nov 2026 11:43.

Barcelona want to prioritise signing a centre-back in the upcoming winter transfer window, but Hansi Flick also wants a upcoming full-back.

Barcelona have won the last two La Liga titles, but have suffered two Champions League failures, in the semi-final against Inter Milan and in the quarter-final against Atletico Madrid.

The defence has always been the main reason for Flick’s side falling short. This has been confirmed again this season, with the heavy defeat away at Paris Saint-Germain (4-2) and the loss to Real Madrid (1-2).

After choosing not to reinforce the defensive axis this summer, Barcelona intend to address the problem in 2027. Flick wants to strengthen his defence with the signings of a centre-back and a full-back, according to Marca.

Recent findings suggest that the Catalan club’s priority is to sign a centre-back. The La Liga champions are working hard and exploring multiple options in that area.

While Josko Gvardiol and Jonathan Tah are options to forget about, Lisandro Martinez has everything of an interesting option, with his contract at Manchester United expiring at the end of the season.

According to recent reports, indeed, Barcelona will have limited resources in the winter transfer window, unless Jules Kounde and Alejandro Balde, who will not be held back if satisfactory offers arrive, leave. Faced with the disappointing performances of the Frenchman and the Spaniard, Barcelona are therefore also in search of a upcoming full-back.

Joao Cancelo (32) is not the club’s future, while the two Masia graduates, Xavi Espart and Brian Farinas, are being used as full-backs but are midfielders by training.

‘Therefore, the arrival of a full-back is urgent and, barring a surprise, it will not happen in January. The aim is to sign one this summer for the following season’ - Marca noted.

Flick will therefore probably have to make do with his full-backs until the end of the season, before a planned arrival in the next summer transfer window. The Spanish outlet mentions right-back Pedro Porro as a way of strengthening that area, but the Spanish world champion is under contract with Tottenham Hotspur until June 2031.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 19 Nov 2026 11:44.

Norwich City welcome Cardiff City to Carrow Road on Saturday afternoon looking to record a fifth successive victory.

At a time when the Canaries sit in 12th position in the Championship table, the Bluebirds trail their hosts by just three points.

While it came as a shock when Norwich lost eight of their opening 11 Championship fixtures in 2026-27, it was equally surprising when they responded with four successive wins before the international break.

With many of their defeats coming by one-goal margins, Philippe Clement would have been anticipating a change in fortunes at some stage.

However, Norwich were sensational between October 24 and November 7, scoring 15 goals in games against Charlton Athletic, Watford, Derby County and Bristol City.

A 4-0 victory at Derby was followed up by a 5-0 triumph at Bristol City, leaving Norwich with the second-best attacking record (32 goals) in the division behind West Ham United.

Although four defeats have been posted from seven fixtures at Carrow Road, the East Anglian side have still scored 13 goals during those matches.

In sharp contrast, Cardiff have only netted six times in seven away fixtures, collecting just two points in the process.

Despite Brian Barry-Murphy's team collecting 14 points across an eight-match period, the bulk of their points are coming at the Cardiff City Stadium.

Incredibly, there were 15 goals in their final two matches before the international break, with four points achieved in matches with West Ham and Burnley that could not have been more different.

After Cardiff gave up a three-goal half-time lead to draw 3-3 with West Ham, they overturned a 4-1 deficit versus Burnley to prevail by a 5-4 scoreline in what is arguably the EFL game of the season so far.

Norwich City Championship form:.

Cardiff City Championship form:.

Barring any fresh fitness complications, Clement could name the same Norwich XI for this fixture.

However, Kenny McLean is in line to return to the squad and will push for a recall in centre-midfield.

Jovon Makama may also be considered for a start, a consequence of the newly-capped England Under-21 international scoring in his last two substitute appearances.

With Joel Bagan serving a one-match for Cardiff, Calum Scanlon is expected to deputise at left-back.

Yousef Salech will also hope to return after scoring a double in the thrilling comeback versus Burnley, with Jack Moylan likely dropping deeper to replace Cian Ashford.

Norwich City possible starting lineup:.

Grimshaw; Stacey, Darling, McConville, Chrisene; Field, Wright; Brooks, Maghoma, Musaba; Kvistgaarden.

Cardiff City possible starting lineup:.

Trott; Ng, Bielik, Fish, Scanlon; Robertson; Tanner, Moylan, Colwill, Willock; Salech.

Although Norwich would have been ruing the start of the international break, we cannot ignore how impressive they were before the two-week rest period. While Cardiff may get on the scoresheet, they could struggle to contain one of the form teams in the division on away territory.

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 11:27 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:55 EST, 16 November 2026.

Manchester United have laid on a private jet for Mauricio Pochettino to fly straight to England in the early hours of Wednesday morning after he finishes work as US national team coach.

Pochettino’s last game in charge is against Haiti in Cincinnati, which kicks off at midnight on Tuesday UK time. The 54-year-old will speak to the media and say farewell to his players before jumping on a plane to Manchester which has been organised by United.

It will enable Pochettino to sleep before he lands in the UK on Wednesday morning ready to go straight to Carrington and start work.

He will be accompanied by first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott.

It has emerged that three other members of his trusted coaching team – assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino – were allowed to travel to Manchester at the weekend after the US won the first leg against Haiti 6-0 in Miami.

Sources indicate that it means that Pochettino’s back-room staff have been able to make a headstart in their preparations for his first game in charge against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday. It is a huge fixture in the calendar for United, but even more so because he takes over a team languishing in the relegation zone.

Man United have laid on a private jet for Mauricio Pochettino to fly straight to England after he finishes work as US national team coach.

Pochettino will take charge of his final match as USA boss in Cincinnati before boarding the direct flight to Manchester.

Pochettino's long-time assistant Jesus Perez is one of three trusted staff members who have already been given permission to travel to Manchester.

Pochettino will be able to work with the players as they begin reporting back from international duty, and is expected to speak to club media before conducting his pre-match press conference on Friday lunchtime.

Speaking ahead of the second leg against Haiti at the TQL Stadium, Pochettino stated: ‘I am with Miguel, Sylvia and Alec and after they are going to join me in Manchester.

‘The next question is where are Jesus, Toni and Sebastiano? They are ahead. After the game (in Miami), they flew to Manchester and they are there in advance. That was the blueprint when we agreed terms with Manchester United and with the US national team.

‘They are there preparing everything because on Wednesday, when we arrive, it’s going to be non-stop and then we start with playing games.’.

#49179. Tech Report: Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying

Tech Report: Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying

📅 03 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (5024 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher.
  • It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together.
  • Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

Sources indicate that eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

Toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian mentioned. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

Still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

Sources indicate that at the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”.

This was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he remarked he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

It has been revealed that “It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”.

Industry observers note that it is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”.

No. 1 ☝️#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/01PqrckQS9.

Sources indicate that tomorrow’s race will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start on the front row together. It is a reasonable run down to turn one and there are overtaking opportunities through the first few corners at Sepang, with it being similar to the configuration in China, with plenty of lines and moves on offer.

Respect between two great champions 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/fbZ6aoKRyw.

Sources indicate that “Very difficult to understand. We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is the different to all the (other) tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi [Antonelli], made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

On Kimi Antonelli’s track limits breach in Q2:.

It has been revealed that “Not good, because Q2 you know you are going to get through. You lose a set [of softs] in a qualifying that is so tight, where we are on the back foot. That is not good.”.

Lewis Hamilton states this is the biggest crowd he has ever seen at Sepang, thanking the fans for making it here today. That is actually a bigger compliment than many watching at home may realise. The traffic this weekend has been horrendous. After 10 years without a race in Malaysia, during which time F1 has grown massively, I think they have forgotten how to do traffic management. Shuttles are inconsistent, taxis can’t get in/out, it’s taking forever just to reach the airport a few kilometres away - some fans have been braving the heat and walking. It took over two hours to get back into Kuala Lumpur last night (48km). My understanding is the Bahrainis are organising the race this year, while local forces are handling the traffic outside the circuit.

In a recent development, “The car has been very good since last week. It is good to come back [from his wrist injury] at such a time and I am enjoying it, fighting for the top three. Even though it was not my finest qualifying session it is a good feeling.

“It is a bit unfortunate we take a penalty on a track where we are that fast but, from eighth, I am confident we can come through the field and come back for a good result.”.

“I love this energy [from the crowd]. Significant, big thank you to Malaysia for welcoming us. It is so hot here. I keep saying it, but that has made it a massive challenge for the tyres, the car, the mechanics in the garage. I am really, really thankful to my team. We made so many changes through all these practice sessions. Because the cars are sliding, the tyres are overheating, it was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot. To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max [Verstappen], who has been so quick all weekend, is great, and I am so grateful.

Recent findings suggest that “I am much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame. Making these tyres last around this track, they are overheating from the get-go. Every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have makes a difference of how far you are going to go. I like to think we have got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I will just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow.”.

A reminder that Isack Hadjar will drop from third to eighth after his grid penalty.

QUALIFYING CLASSIFICATIONCan't wait for Sunday! 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/qqi8hPDcKA.

Sources indicate that “It is fantastic. We have been trying many grand prix to get pole. Sometimes a bit closer than others but to finally get it, from where we started the season, pretty incredible. I am happy with today and, for sure, I am going to try and win tomorrow. When you start first, that is the target.”.

Big disappointment that for Russell. After his win in Baku, where he mentioned he finally felt hooked up to the car, he was desperate to build the momentum. P8, four places behind Antonelli, was not what he would have had in mind. Has it all to do in the race tomorrow.

According to recent reports, excellent (though not unexpected) pole for Verstappen, and a very good P2 for Hamilton. Could be some fireworks on the front row tomorrow.

*Hadjar’s three-place grid penalty will drop him down to eighth place for the race tomorrow.

Recent findings suggest that neither of the Red Bulls can improve in the first sector but it is those behind them who need significant improvements. The two Ferraris are going along nicely at the start of their final flying laps. Hadjar is unable to improve despite a purple final sector. Verstappen then goes fastest in the final sector and improves his advantage at the top.

Hamilton meanwhile went fastest in the middle sector and goes second fastest overall. Piastri cannot improve but stays ahead of Russell.

Norris is the final man across the line but is only fast enough for P6. That means that Verstappen takes pole in Malaysia, which is the first time this season that Red Bull have taken pole position. Hamilton is second with Hadjar third, although the Frenchman has a five-place grid penalty.

In a recent development, MAX VERSTAPPEN TAKES POLE FOR THE BAHRAIN GRAND PRIX IN MALAYSIA!! 👊#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/NgtaCAZacL.

The two Red Bulls, who are one and two at the moment, will be the first two drivers across the line on these final efforts.

Recent findings suggest that the other nine drivers in Q3 are in the pits so young Antonelli has the track to himself as he sets his one and only flying lap of Q3. He is over four tenths down on Verstappen through the first sector and has plenty of work to do.

The championship leader sets a decent middle sector where he loses no more time to Verstappen. As it stands he would put himself third before the others do their final runs. He comes across the line in P3 but will have the likes of Hamilton, Piastri, Leclerc, Norris and Russell trying to surpass him.

Russell is the first across the line and sets a time of a 1:36.032. He does not last long at the top as he is immediately displaced by Hadjar, who is half a second quicker.

Hamilton then comes over the line in second, just ahead of his teammate Leclerc. Piastri puts himself between the two Ferraris.

What about Verstappen? The man who won here the last time we were in Malaysia continues his great form today and goes quickest by more than three tenths.

Antonelli now heads out and will have the track to himself really. This is going to be the championship leader’s only flying lap of Q3.

Russell is the first man to head out for his first flying lap in Q3. Antonelli has remained in the pits with just one upcoming set of softs remaining. Verstappen, who right now feels like the favourite for pole, will be one of the last across the line in these first attempts of Q3.

The fight for pole position in Sepang begins now as the green light is on at the end of the pit lane to get Q3 going.

Antonelli, due to that lap time deletion in Q2, has just one latest set of softs for Q3, which could prove costly in his attempts to try and take pole.

P12 the best qualifying result of the season for Alonso. It was only his second time in Q2 after Hungary (P16).

Recent findings suggest that I should add, P14 was also Lance Stroll’s best qualifying result of the season. His first outing in Q2 this year.

11. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls)12. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)13. Carlos Sainz (Williams)14. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls).

With grid penalties already on their way, neither Colapinto nor Lindblad set lap times in Q2.

Sources indicate that verstappen, Leclerc, Piastri, Norris, Hadjar and Russell all remain in the pits. A bit of a risk for Russell down in eighth but his time should be enough to get into Q3.

Lindblad, who will start tomorrow’s race at the back of the grid after penalties, gives his teammate Lawson a tow down the back straight and it works as Lawson just sneaks into the top ten.

Can Bortoleto get back ahead though of Lawson? Yes he can and he will take the final place in Q3. Lawson thought he might be through but the tow was not enough.

Lindblad, who's taking a grid penalty for Sunday's race, gave team mate Lawson a tow but it wasn't quite enough to send the Kiwi into Q3#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/IMlrqg4ENv.

Industry observers note that as the young Italian starts his flying lap, there is no-one else out on track so no traffic. He is a lot more cautious at turn six this time than last time, when he had his lap time deleted.

He has not set blistering first and second sector times but a purple final sector puts him into second and the Italian is safely into Q3.

Plenty of other drivers are now heading around the track for their final flying laps of Q2.

Sources indicate that 11. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)12. Carlos Sainz (Williams)13. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes)14. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin).

According to recent reports, mercedes have put a brand upcoming set of softs onto Antonelli’s car as he heads out promptly, with no lap time to his name so far. Antonelli is still disputing the lap deletion over team radio but his team tell him the images show he exceeded track limits. This is now a lot of pressure on the championship leader; any mistake now and he will not make Q3. His teammate Russell is only in seventh.

Antonelli was fourth fastest but has had his lap time deleted for exceeding track limits at turn six. That is a significant moment in Q2 and could prove problematic if he gets into Q3. Antonelli appeared to be confused when he was told about his lap deletion over team radio but the on-board view looked pretty clear-cut.

Piastri then comes across the line in third.

Here's the moment Kimi ran wide 👀#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/E0VdWdBt8x.

The Dutchman looks in a great spot at the moment to take pole position today and his 1:35.696 is very quick. He is nearly four tenths quicker than Antonelli.

According to recent reports, how about the Ferraris? Leclerc was quickest in the middle sector but is nearly three tenths down on Verstappen. Hamilton puts himself into third place. Russell is more than half a second down on Verstappen.

Verstappen has been shown a black and white flag for driving unnecessarily slowly. I doubt he will get a grid penalty for that but it will be a warning for the Dutchman.

Anyway, the drivers, other than Colapinto and Alonso, are on flying laps, with Verstappen currently fastest inthe first sector.

Sources indicate that the green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and the second part of qualifying is under way. Like the start of Q1, it is hardly a stampede to go out.

Sources indicate that 17. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi)18. Oliver Bearman (Haas)19. Esteban Ocon (Haas)20. Alex Albon (Williams)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac).

In a recent development, the Aston Martin of Stroll improves significantly from 20th and is set to make Q2, as is his teammate Alonso. A bit of a surprise to see the Aston Martins improve and make it into Q2.

Recent findings suggest that go Fernando! 🤩 Go Lance! 🤩First double Q2 appearance this season 🙌#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/xjiWYv6ycr.

Sources indicate that that has seen the Audi of Hulkenberg drop into the drop zone and the German is out. For contrast, his teammate improves to go into eighth place! Hulkenberg had a substantial lock up into turn 14, which proved very costly.

It has been revealed that as it stands, eight of the top nine are remaining in the garage. Russell is in ninth and has not gone out but Gasly above him in eighth has. You would imagine Russell is perfectly safe.

17. Esteban Ocon (Haas)18. Alex Albon (Williams)19. Oliver Bearman (Haas)20. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac).

Ocon, in 17th, is quite far off Hulkenberg in 16th and needs more than four tenths to usurp him.

It has been revealed that the screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he indicates Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

In a recent development, “Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external tech giant who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

According to recent reports, he added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”.

The two Ferraris are on medium tyres but Leclerc still puts himself into second place. He is then displaced by Hamilton, who slots in behind Verstappen. Good times from the Ferraris on the mediums.

According to recent reports, what about the McLarens? Norris goes sixth fastest but is more than six tenths down on Verstappen. Then comes Piastri, who goes fourth fastest, just under four tenths off Verstappen.

Arguably the three favourites for pole; Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen, are all on flying laps.

The first sector goes the way of Verstappen, who is purple, and then the Dutchman goes purple in the middle sector.

Sources indicate that antonelli is two tenths faster than his teammate Russell but Verstappen is over half a second quicker than the Mercedes. Hadjar is then second fastest to show the pace in the Red Bull this weekend.

Sources indicate that most of the teams waited and waited to come out and then suddenly lots of drivers are sent out, resulting in a queue in the pits! With the high track temperatures and high degradation, the drivers are crawling around on their out laps to preserve these soft tyres.

In a recent development, bumper to bumper in the pit lane! #F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/ff8JO9kB1g.

Sources indicate that the two Haas drivers have a free track to themselves whilst everyone else bides their time. In theory, as the hour of qualifying goes on, the track temperature should decrease and the more rubber that is laid down the faster the track should get.

Finally, just before the two Haas drivers finish their first flying laps, the rest of the grid is starting to emerge, led by the Mercedes duo.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and Q1 is officially under way. The two Haas drivers are the first to head out. Other than that, it is a quiet start to Q1.

Industry observers note that the top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

Not long to wait now until qualifying begins. It is hot, humid and dry in Sepang right now. As we know in Malaysia, the weather can change swiftly and thunderstorms can roll in quite quickly but it looks like today’s qualifying will be a dry one. This will be one of if not the hottest qualifying sessions of the season, so much so that we are seeing umbrellas going up to get some shade from the sun rather than sheltering from any rain.

This will be crucial to consider after qualifying finishes as there will be some shuffling around:.

Isack Hadjar (Red Bull): five-place grid penalty- latest internal combustion engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): ten-place grid penalty- new engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): five-place grid penalty- causing a collision in BakuArvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls): back of the grid- complete power unit change.

Hadjar has looked good since returning from his wrist injury so could be fighting it out near the front of the grid, although his five-place penalty will drop him down. We know Lindblad will be at the back and is very likely to be joined there by Colapinto, who is not going to be qualifying high up in the top ten in his Alpine.

Haas have announced that Frenchman Esteban Ocon will leave at the end of this season. Ocon now faces an uncertain future, with it difficult to see a spot for him on the F1 grid next season. There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara presently leads the Formula 2 championship.

TGR Haas F1 Team and Esteban Ocon will part ways at the conclusion of the 2026 season. With plenty of racing ahead, our focus remains on working together to maximize every opportunity through to the final race of the year.#HaasF1 #F1 pic.twitter.com/4iQAuqnSyA.

According to recent reports, aston Martin have now confirmed their driver line-up for next season, retaining both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. There had been reports that Alonso had been contemplating retirement but the 45-year-old will continue into another season.

In a recent development, aston Martin Aramco confirms Lance and Fernando will continue as the team's drivers in 2027. Read more: ​https://t.co/ePyjJdyAIB pic.twitter.com/VogFUEbNxy.

Other than the second seat alongside Ollie Bearman at Haas, the only other team to keep an eye on is Racing Bulls, with no definite confirmation on their exact driver line-up for next season.

According to recent reports, ferrari this week have publicly backed their team principal Frederic Vasseur, amid speculation over the Frenchman’s position and comments made by former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who stated the job at Ferrari would be a “dream job”. Ferrari, who sit second in the constructors’ standings, have not won the drivers’ championship since 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) and the constructors’ since 2008. Here is a snippet from Tom Cary’s piece on the matter:.

In a hastily convened media call on Tuesday morning, Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communication officer, mentioned the Scuderia had decided to concern a vote of confidence in Vasseur in response “not just to the story of Mr Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred”.

Industry observers note that “Ferrari has made its choices,” Conti stated. “We have confidence – full confidence – in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.

“At this time, it’s really crucial that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.”.

“It is great to be back [in Malaysia]. I am really enjoying the track. We have had some wonderful races here over time. It is actually the 20th time we have been here, it started in 1999, and it is really exciting to be back. I really enjoyed getting out on the track and watching the cars closely.

“The drivers are super fit and they have some cooling but it is not easy. But you almost cannot get enough fluid through your body before your stomach gives up. Having this race and Singapore back-to-back increases that challenge.”.

Especially with the massive upgrade they have brought this weekend, Mercedes’ lead at the summit is looking unassailable right now.

It has been revealed that almost nine years ago to the day, Max Verstappen took just his second race victory in Formula 1. Lewis Hamilton, who took pole position, and Daniel Ricciardo joined Verstappen on the podium. Despite being nine years ago, plenty of drivers still on the grid were racing that weekend. Here they are and who they were racing for:.

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes) Esteban Ocon (Force India)Nico Hulkenberg (Renault)Sergio Perez (Force India)Fernando Alonso (McLaren)Lance Stroll (Williams)Carlos Sainz (Toro Rosso)Pierre Gasly (Toro Rosso).

According to recent reports, with Russell winning in Baku and Antonelli finishing fifth, the latter’s championship lead was cut to 66 points. If Russell is going to usurp his teammate, he is going to need a few more similar results to last weekend due to the size of Antonelli’s lead. If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

Formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

Last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

Sources indicate that verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Earlier today, championship leader Antonelli was nearly three tenths clear of the field in third practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a new floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car patch since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

This race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).
